body.statement: The horizon-adaptive feasible sets contain their deepest-pool counterparts, so \(W_{\mathrm{nested}}\le W_{\mathrm{deep}}\) and \(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\le\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\) for every admissible fixed design.
body.justification: This is a sanity and boundary corollary of feasible-set inclusion, included without novelty credit.
body.gap: No literature gap is claimed for this tautological feasible-set implication; BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022 supplies only the shrinking-donor-set and common-support geometry anchor.
body.consumer: The boundary check lets \texttt{augsynth::multisynth} verify that enabling horizon-adaptive support cannot worsen the declared honest-width objective.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal E\), \(0\le h\le K\).  If \(i\in D_{jK}\), then the definition of the donor sets gives
\[
T_i>T_j+K\ge T_j+h,
\]
and hence \(i\in D_{jh}\).  Therefore
\[
D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\qquad\text{for every }(j,h)\in\mathcal E.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:donor-feasibility}\) states that every \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty, so all deepest-pool simplexes below are nonempty.  Moreover, if \(v\in\Delta(D_{jK})\), then \(v_i\ge0\), \(v_i=0\) for \(i\notin D_{jK}\), and \(\sum_{i\in D_{jK}}v_i=1\).  The displayed set inclusion implies that \(v_i=0\) also for every \(i\notin D_{jh}\), while
\[
\sum_{i\in D_{jh}}v_i
=\sum_{i\in D_{jK}}v_i+
  \sum_{i\in D_{jh}\setminus D_{jK}}v_i
=1.
\]
Thus \(\Delta(D_{jK})\subseteq\Delta(D_{jh})\) for each coordinate.  Taking the product over \(\mathcal E\), as prescribed by the definition of \(\mathcal F_s\), yields
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}.
\]

For the exact-width comparison, let \(\mathcal H_s\) be the set of pairs \((w,\ell)\) satisfying all constraints in \(\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}\) under support rule \(s\).  Concretely, membership requires \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), \(\ell\in[0,\infty)^M\), determinism of \(w\) and \(\ell\) conditional on the fixed inputs, and
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}
P\!\left\{
\left|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e\right|\le\ell_e
\text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E
\right\}\ge1-\alpha.
\]
The last three requirements and the objective \(\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e\) do not depend on \(s\).  Hence the feasible-set inclusion just proved gives
\[
\mathcal H_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal H_{\mathrm{nested}}.
\]
Monotonicity of an infimum under enlargement of its feasible set, applied directly to \(\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}\), now gives
\[
W_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{nested}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
\le
\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{deep}}}
  \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
=W_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\]
This argument remains valid if an honesty-feasible set is empty, using the extended-value convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\) already allowed by the codomain of \(W_s\).

For the SOCP comparison, let \(\mathcal S_s\) denote the feasible set of quadruples \((w,u,v,g)\) in \(\texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}\).  Every constraint other than \(w\in\mathcal F_s\) is the same for the two support rules: for every \((j,h)\in\mathcal E\),
\[
\left\|x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right\|_2\le u_{jh},
\qquad
\left\|R_Qa_{jh}(w)\right\|_2\le v_{jh},
\qquad
Lu_{jh}+\delta+z_Bv_{jh}\le g.
\]
Consequently, \(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}\) implies
\[
\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}.
\]
The objective is the same scalar \(g\) on both sets.  Therefore, by the minimization in \(\texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}\),
\[
\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
=\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}}g
\le
\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}}g
=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\]
Together, the two inequalities prove the proposition for every admissible fixed design.
